Goal: Publish complete listings and let buyers find available products and place orders.
Hold authorized funds and release seller payout only under the scenario conditions.
Capture independent inspection evidence, buyer decisions, and authorized dispute resolutions.
Limit access to order, escrow, inspection, and dispute records by role.

Summary: Create and publish a complete listing
User Story: As a seller, I want to publish a listing with its required product details so buyers can review the item before ordering.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a seller supplies a title, description, condition, photographs, and asking price, when the seller publishes, then the system saves the listing and marks it available. If any required field is missing, publication is rejected and the listing is not shown as available.

User Story: As a buyer, I want to view published available listings so I can choose an item to order.
Acceptance Criteria: Given published listings exist, when a buyer opens the listing view, then available listings are shown with title, condition, photographs, and asking price. Listings that are unavailable are not offered for ordering.

Summary: Place an order and show the amount due
User Story: As an authenticated buyer, I want to order an available listing and see the order ID and total amount due so I can identify and pay for the transaction.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the buyer selects a published available listing, when the order is placed, then one order is created for that buyer and listing and the order ID and total amount are displayed. An unavailable listing cannot create an order.

User Story: As a buyer, I want my authorized payment held in escrow while inspection is pending so the seller is not paid before the release conditions are met.
Acceptance Criteria: Given payment is authorized for an order, when the payment is recorded, then the ledger shows funds held and the order state becomes Under Inspection. Seller payout is rejected until inspector verification and buyer sign-off are both recorded.

User Story: As the inspector assigned to an order, I want to submit a Pass or Fail outcome with findings and evidence so the buyer can evaluate the item.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an inspector is assigned to the order, when that inspector submits an outcome, findings, evidence, and submission time, then the report is saved and the state becomes Awaiting Buyer Sign-Off. An unassigned user cannot submit it.

Summary: Review report and record buyer decision
User Story: As the buyer, I want to review the inspection report and either sign off or open a dispute so the order follows my decision.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the order is Awaiting Buyer Sign-Off, when the buyer reviews the report, then the buyer can record sign-off or open a dispute and the decision is linked to the order. Only that order's buyer can decide.

Summary: Open a dispute and retain the escrow hold
User Story: As a buyer, I want to open a dispute about a failed inspection or condition disagreement so funds stay protected during review.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a failed inspection or buyer dispute, when the case is opened, then a dispute case is linked to the order and escrow remains held. Seller payout stays blocked while the dispute is active.

User Story: As an authorized dispute agent, I want to record the resolution of an active case so there is an accountable decision before the hold is cleared.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an active dispute, when an authorized dispute agent records a resolution, then the decision, agent, and time are saved and the case leaves active investigation. An unauthorized user cannot resolve it. No refund or payout outcome is assumed because Lab 1 does not specify one.

Summary: Release seller payout only after both conditions
User Story: As a seller, I want payout released only after a passing inspection and buyer sign-off so the escrow rules are enforced.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a passing inspection and buyer sign-off with no active dispute, when payout is requested, then one payout can be released. If either condition is absent, the report failed, or a dispute is active, payout is rejected and funds remain held.

Summary: Freeze disputed funds within the performance target
User Story: As a dispute investigator, I want escrow to freeze immediately when a dispute is opened so funds cannot leave during investigation.
Acceptance Criteria: Under 500 concurrent order actions, the 95th-percentile time from dispute-ticket creation to escrow freeze is at most 2 seconds. All seller withdrawal attempts are rejected while the related ticket is active. Record the performance test result.

User Story: As a marketplace participant, I want access to orders, escrow records, inspection reports, and dispute cases limited by my role so private transaction data stays protected.
Acceptance Criteria: For buyer, seller, assigned-inspector, dispute-agent, and payment-service roles, permitted access succeeds and unrelated access is denied. In 30 role and cross-account cases, no protected fields are returned to unauthorized requests and access outcomes are recorded.
